title: Choosing LLMs for Strategic Agent Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.18354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Game-theoretic benchmarks claim that large language model (LLM) strategic decision-making varies across game types, interaction structures, and capability dimensions. However, they only evaluate strategic performance across individual fixed models. In parallel, contemporary LLM routers pick models under quality-cost trade-offs, but with no notion of a strategic structure. They do not account for an opponent that might be unknown, and that can adapt over time and shift the feedback signal. To address this, we extend the game-theoretic evaluations and define strategic selection as the meta game layered on top of the base game. In each round, a strategic selector fields an LLM from a portfolio of models to navigate a game payoff matrix that is latent and learned online. translated_title: 为策略性智能体交互选择大语言模型
translated_abstract: 博弈论基准测试声称，大语言模型（LLM）的策略性决策在不同博弈类型、交互结构和能力维度上存在差异。然而，这些基准测试仅评估单个固定模型的策略性表现。与此同时，当代的LLM路由器在质量-成本权衡下选择模型，但对策略结构没有任何概念。它们没有考虑到对手可能是未知的，且对手可以随时间适应并改变反馈信号。为解决这一问题，我们扩展了博弈论评估，并将策略性选择定义为叠加在基础博弈之上的元博弈。在每一轮中，策略性选择器从模型组合中派出一个LLM，来应对一个潜在的、需在线学习的博弈收益矩阵。我们发现评估信号是依赖于具体博弈的，并且与传统基准测试相比，提取可靠的信号需要多得多的种子运行次数N。
tldr: 该论文提出将“策略性选择”定义为叠加在基础博弈之上的元博弈，使选择器能够从模型组合中动态选择LLM，以应对未知且会随时间适应变化的对手，从而将博弈论评估从固定模型比较扩展到在线学习的潜在收益矩阵场景。
en_tdlr: This paper defines strategic selection as a meta-game layered on top of the base game, where a selector dynamically fields LLMs from a portfolio to navigate latent, online-learned payoff matrices against unknown and adaptive opponents, extending game-theoretic evaluations beyond fixed model comparisons.
